body:
Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33292

Mirror issue: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/1918

## What changed

- Add the missing base `CustomOp.forward_xpu()` fallback to `forward_native()` in the multimodal generation runtime.
- Add focused regression coverage for native-only subclasses, explicit XPU overrides, and subclasses with no backend implementation.
- Include the required investigation report and raw before/after evidence under `reports/j-0f02b0ec022d/`.

## Reproduction and validation

Before the production change, the new focused test records 2 failures at construction with the reported missing-`forward_xpu` `AttributeError` and 1 passing explicit-override case:

```bash
/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-0f02b0ec022d/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_custom_op.py
```

After restoring the fix, the same command reports `3 passed`. The issue-specific standalone reproduction also changes from construction-time `AttributeError` to selecting `forward_xpu` and returning the expected native result.

## Limitations

- No Intel XPU hardware or torch XPU build was available. The assigned accelerator is one AMD Instinct MI350X (`gfx950`), which cannot qualify Intel XPU execution, so no GPU execution is claimed.
- Full multimodal model loading, model weights, and architecture-level semantic behavior were not tested. The regression directly validates the reported construction and dispatch contract.
- The prepared interpreter does not include `ruff`; that unavailable check is recorded in `result.json` and the raw logs.
- No native rebuild was needed because this is a Python-only dispatch change.
title: fix(multimodal_gen): add default XPU custom op fallback
